slo_title: Understand Circular Singly Linked Lists - Insertion

mcq.q: In a singly linked list, how do you handle deletion at the middle when the list has an even number of nodes
A railway booking system stores ticket reservations in a circular singly linked list. If a new reservation is added between two existing reservations, what needs to be adjusted

options.A: The previous reservation’s next pointer should point to the new reservation
options.B: The list should be reversed before insertion
options.C: The head pointer should be moved
options.D: The last reservation should be deleted

mcq.answer_text: The previous reservation’s next pointer should point to the new reservation

mcq.q: An online food ordering system maintains active orders in a circular singly linked list. A new order is placed at the end. What must be updated

options.A: The new node’s next pointer must point to the head
options.B: The first order should be deleted
options.C: The system should convert the list into a doubly linked list
options.D: The order must be inserted at the second position

mcq.answer_text: The new node’s next pointer must point to the head

mcq.q: What is the time complexity of deleting a node from the middle of a singly linked list
If a node is deleted from the middle of a singly linked list, what happens to the structure of the list

options.B: The previous node’s next pointer is updated to the next node of the deleted node

mcq.answer_text: The previous node’s next pointer is updated to the next node of the deleted node
